title: Reported Speech: Statements & Tense Backshift
grammarTitle: Reported Speech — Part 1: Statements, Tense Shifts & Say vs Tell
grammarNote: Reported speech (косвенная речь) — это способ передать слова другого человека без их точного цитирования. В английском языке при переводе прямой речи в косвенную происходит так называемый backshift (сдвиг времени назад): глаголы становятся более «далёкими» от настоящего. Но у этого правила есть важные исключения.

grammarExtra.title: SAY vs TELL — the essential difference

rows.example: "She SAID that she was tired." ✅ / "She SAID she was going." ✅ / "He SAID nothing." ✅
"She SAID TO me that she was tired." ✅ (not "She said me that..." ✗)
"She TOLD ME that she was tired." ✅ / "He TOLD US the news." ✅ / "She told him." ✅
✅ "She TOLD ME / HIM / US that..." — TELL always needs a person object! ✅
"She EXPLAINED TO ME that..." / "He MENTIONED (to me) that..." / "She ADMITTED (to us) that..."

grammarExtra.title: Time and place shifts in reported speech

rows.example: "I am working now." → She said she was working THEN.
"I saw him today." → He said he had seen him THAT DAY.

rows.form: yesterday → the day before / the previous day
rows.example: "She left yesterday." → He said she had left THE DAY BEFORE.

rows.form: tomorrow → the next day / the following day
rows.example: "I'll come tomorrow." → She said she would come THE NEXT DAY.
"I'm busy this week." → He said he was busy THAT WEEK.
"I live here." → She said she lived THERE.
"I love this city." → He said he loved THAT city.
"I arrived two days ago." → She said she had arrived two days BEFORE.

grammarExtra.title: When you do NOT need to backshift

rows.form: 1. Still true at time of reporting
rows.example: "The sun rises in the east." → She said the sun RISES in the east. (universal truth — no shift needed) ✅
"I'm tired." → She says she's tired. (reporting instantly — no shift) ✅
"I'll be there at 8." → He says he'll be there at 8. (present reporting = no shift) ✅
"I would help." → She said she would help. (no further shift — already past modal) ✅
"If I had time, I could come." → He said if he had time, he could come. ✅
In informal speech, backshift is often optional: "She said she is tired." is acceptable. ✅

grammarExtra.title: Pronoun and tense changes — the full picture in one example

rows.form: DIRECT: "I've been working here for two years. I know the manager well and I'll stay."
rows.example: Kamila (to Rustam)

rows.form: REPORTED: She said (that) she had been working THERE for two years, (that) SHE knew the manager well and (that) SHE would stay.
rows.example: Pronoun: I→she. Place: here→there. PPC→PPP Cont. PS→PS (know=still true OR PS). will→would.

rows.form: Key decision: which shifts to apply?
rows.example: Consider: Is it still true? How long ago? What style? All affect which tense you choose. ✅
say, tell, admit, claim, complain, explain, insist, promise, reply, report, state ✅

rows.form: "She admitted THAT she had made a mistake."
rows.example: "He claimed THAT he had never seen the document." ✅
"He promised THAT he would return it." ✅
promise to, offer to, refuse to, agree to, claim to, pretend to ✅

rows.form: "She promised TO help." / "He refused TO come."
rows.example: "She agreed TO meet at 3." / "He pretended TO be asleep." ✅

grammarTip:
Reported Speech — Statements:

📌 Backshift: глагол «сдвигается назад»
PS → PP → Past Perfect
PC → Past Continuous
PPS → Past Perfect Simple
PPC → Past Perfect Continuous
will → would · can → could · may → might · must → had to

📌 SAY vs TELL:
Say: "She SAID (that) she was tired." (no object needed)
Tell: "She TOLD ME (that) she was tired." (ALWAYS + object!)
✗ "She told that..." → ✅ "She told him/me/us that..."

📌 Time/place shifts:
now → then · today → that day
tomorrow → the next day · here → there

📌 When NOT to shift:
→ Universal truths (sun rises in east)
→ Reporting immediately
→ would/could/might/should — already past!
→ Still true at the moment of reporting

📌 B1 Reporting verbs + that:
admit / claim / insist / promise / explain / complain
→ + to-inf: promise to / agree to / refuse to / offer to

exercises.instruction: Choose the correct reported speech form.
exercises.text: Amir said: "I am studying machine learning." → He said he ___ machine learning.
exercises.hint: Present Continuous → Past Continuous in reported speech. "I am studying" → he said he WAS STUDYING. ✅

exercises.text: Kamila said: "I have never been to Istanbul." → She said she ___ to Istanbul.
exercises.hint: Present Perfect → Past Perfect. "have never been" → HAD NEVER BEEN. ✅

exercises.text: "She ___ me that the lecture had been cancelled."
exercises.hint: "TOLD ME" — TELL always needs a person object (me/him/her/us). "Said me" ✗ is wrong! ✅

exercises.text: Rustam said: "I will help you tomorrow." → He said he ___ help me the next day.
exercises.hint: will → WOULD in reported speech. "I will help" → he said he WOULD HELP. ✅

exercises.instruction: Report the sentence with time shift.
exercises.text: She said: "I saw him today." → She said she had seen him ___.
exercises.hint: "today" → "THAT DAY" in reported speech. ✅

exercises.text: She said: "The capital of Kazakhstan is Nur-Sultan." → She said the capital of Kazakhstan ___ Nur-Sultan.
exercises.hint: Universal or permanent facts don't REQUIRE backshift. "Is" (still true) is also correct. Both acceptable. ✅

exercises.instruction: Choose the correct reported form for Past Simple.
exercises.text: "I went to Almaty last week." → He said he ___ to Almaty the week before.
exercises.hint: Past Simple → Past Perfect in formal reported speech. "went" → HAD GONE. ✅

exercises.instruction: Choose the correct modal — no shift needed.
exercises.text: "I could try to help you." → He said he ___ try to help me.
exercises.hint: "could" is ALREADY a past modal — NO further shift. "He said he COULD try." ✅

exercises.instruction: Report using the correct reporting verb structure.
exercises.text: Zhibek said: "I will definitely finish the project." → She ___ finish the project.
exercises.hint: promise + TO + infinitive. "She PROMISED TO finish the project." ✅ (Also possible: "promised that she would finish")

exercises.text: "I live here in Uralsk." → She said she lived ___ in Uralsk.
exercises.hint: "here" → "THERE" in reported speech when the location has changed. ✅

exercises.text: "I've been waiting for an hour." → She said she ___ for an hour.
exercises.hint: Present Perfect Continuous → Past Perfect Continuous. "have been waiting" → HAD BEEN WAITING. ✅

exercises.text: "I didn't take the money," he said. → He ___ taking the money.
exercises.hint: "denied" + gerund = denied TAKING. Better than "said" for this meaning. "He DENIED TAKING the money." ✅

exercises.text: "I'm very tired and I can't come today." → She said she ___ very tired and she ___ come that day.
exercises.hint: PS→PS (am→was), can→could → can't→couldn't, today→that day. "She said she WAS very tired and she COULDN'T come THAT DAY." ✅

exercises.instruction: Choose the correct form of "tell" or "say".
exercises.text: "___ that she would be late." (No object mentioned)
exercises.hint: No object → SAY. "She SAID that she would be late." ✅ "She told that..." ✗ — TELL needs an object (told me/him/us). ✅

exercises.text: "I must finish this by Friday." → He said he ___ finish it by Friday.
exercises.hint: "must" (obligation) → "HAD TO" in reported speech. "He said he HAD TO finish it by Friday." ✅

exercises.text: "When I was studying, I had already realised I wanted to change direction." → She said that when she ___ studying, she ___ already ___ she wanted to change direction.
exercises.hint: PC→PPC ("was studying"→"had been studying"), PP stays PP ("had already realised"→"had already realised"). ✅

exercises.text: Find the WRONG reported form.
opts: "She said she was leaving." (was leaving = correct)
"He said he had been working there." (correct)
"She said she can help." (WRONG — should be "could")
exercises.correct: "She said she can help." (WRONG — should be "could")
exercises.hint: "can" → "COULD" in reported speech. "She said she CAN help." ✗ → ✅ "She said she COULD help." ✅

exercises.instruction: Choose the correct reporting verb + structure.
exercises.text: Daniyar: "I'm sorry, I was wrong." → He ___ making a mistake.
exercises.hint: "admit" + gerund. "He ADMITTED MAKING a mistake." ✅ (Also: admitted that he had been wrong)

exercises.text: "She said she's ready now." vs "She said she was ready then." — which is acceptable?
opts: Both — present tense acceptable if still true or recent
exercises.correct: Both — present tense acceptable if still true or recent
exercises.hint: Backshift is REQUIRED in formal written English but optional in informal speech when the situation is still current. ✅

exercises.text: "I may be late tomorrow," she said. → She said she might be late tomorrow.
opts: Wrong — "tomorrow" should shift to "the next day"
exercises.correct: Wrong — "tomorrow" should shift to "the next day"
exercises.hint: "tomorrow" → "THE NEXT DAY" in reported speech. ✅ "She said she might be late THE NEXT DAY." ✅

opts: Shifting verbs one tense "further back" into the past
questions.correct: Shifting verbs one tense "further back" into the past
questions.hint: Backshift = tenses move one step further back when reporting past speech. PS→PP, PC→PPC, will→would, etc. ✅

questions.text: "She said she is tired." — Is this acceptable?
opts: Yes — in informal speech when the situation is still current
questions.correct: Yes — in informal speech when the situation is still current
questions.hint: In informal speech, backshift is optional if the situation is still true. Both "is" and "was" can be correct. ✅
Present Perfect → Past Perfect. "has/have finished" → HAD FINISHED. ✅

questions.text: "She told that she was leaving." — What is wrong?
questions.hint: ✅ "She TOLD US/ME that she was leaving." — TELL always needs a person object! ✅

questions.text: "I can help." → He said he ___ help.
questions.hint: "can" → "could" in reported speech. "He said he COULD help." ✅

questions.text: "I must leave now." → She said she ___ leave.
"I would help if I could." → He said he ___ help if he ___.
questions.hint: "would" and "could" are ALREADY past modals — NO further shift. ✅

questions.text: "I'm studying here now." → She said she ___ studying ___ then.
questions.hint: PC→PC (was studying), here→there, now→then. "She said she WAS STUDYING THERE THEN." ✅

questions.text: Which sentence does NOT require backshift?
questions.hint: Universal facts/truths don't require backshift. "She said the earth orbits the sun." ✅ (or "orbited" — both acceptable)

questions.text: "I've been working here for two years." → He said he ___ there for two years.
questions.hint: PPC → Past Perfect Continuous. "has been working" → HAD BEEN WORKING. ✅

questions.text: "I refuse to pay." → She said she ___ pay.
questions.hint: "refuse" + to + infinitive. "She said she REFUSED TO pay." ✅ (Also: "she refused to pay" = correct reported form)

questions.text: Which reporting verb needs a GERUND?
questions.hint: "deny" + GERUND. "He DENIED TAKING the money." ✅ (Not "denied to take." "Deny" = gerund only, not infinitive) ✅

questions.text: "I said her that I was coming." — What is wrong?
opts: "said her" is wrong — should be "said to her" or "told her"
questions.correct: "said her" is wrong — should be "said to her" or "told her"
questions.hint: ✅ "I said TO HER that..." or "I TOLD HER that..." — never "said her." ✅

questions.text: "She may arrive late." → He said she ___ arrive late.
questions.hint: "may" → "might" in reported speech. "He said she MIGHT arrive late." ✅

questions.text: Which shows ALL shifts applied correctly?
opts: "She said she had been working there when he had called."
"He said he will help me tomorrow."
questions.correct: "She said she had been working there when he had called."
questions.hint: had been working (PPC✅) + there (here→there✅) + had called (PS→PP✅). All shifts correct. ✅
